title: One read-write lock for every repository

blocks.text: The page's violation gives each repository its own copy of the read-write locking:

Its fix is one shared wrapper, `ReadWriteLockedResource<T>`: every repository uses it, so moving from `ReentrantReadWriteLock` to another lock is a change in one class. `UserRepository` and `ProductRepository` below already use it. Complete the wrapper:

items: `read(readAction)` applies the action to the resource under the **read** lock and returns its result. **Readers do not block each other**: two reads run at the same time;
`writeVoid(writeAction)` applies the action under the **write** lock, which **holds back every reader** until the write is done;
each lock is released in a `finally` block;
a `null` resource is refused by the constructor, and a `null` action by `read` or `writeVoid`, with `NullPointerException` **before any locking happens**.
a new `UserRepository` returns an empty list from `getAllUsers()`; after `addUser("u-1", "Ann")`, `getUser("u-1")` is `"Ann"`, and `getUser("u-9")` is `null`;
two threads that each call `read` can both be inside their read actions at once;
while a writer is inside `writeVoid`, a thread calling `read` waits, then sees the writer's change;

cases.says: Both repositories store and read back through the shared wrapper.
Two readers are inside their read actions at the same time.
A reader waits while a writer is inside writeVoid.
A null resource is refused by the constructor, not later.
read(null) throws NullPointerException at once, even while a writer holds the lock: the check comes before any locking.
When a read action throws, its exception reaches the caller and the read lock is released: a later write goes through.

concepts: A null resource or a null action is refused at once, before any locking happens.
Under a read-write lock, readers do not block each other, while a writer blocks everyone.
One ReadWriteLockedResource wrapper gives every repository the same locking, so a change of lock strategy is one edit.
